definition: ἔνοχος, -ον (= ἐνεχόμενος),  (in LXX for רָשַׁע hi., etc. ;] __1. held in, bound by: with genitive (cl. with dative), δουλείας, Heb.2:15.  __2. In law-phrases  __(a) liable to a charge or action (cl. with dative, of crime): with dative, of the tribunal (MM, Exp., xiii), Mat.5:21-22; before εἰς (Field, Notes, 4 f.), Mat.5:22  __(b) with genitive, of the punishment (Gen.26:11): θανάτου, Mat.26:66, Mrk.14:64;  __(with) with genitive (cl. with dative„ rarely with prep.; MM, Exp., xiii), of the crime  (2Ma.13:6): Mrk.3:29;  __(d) with genitive, of the thing injured, guilty (absol., in Cl.): 1Co.11:27, Jas.2:10 (cf. Isa.54:17; DB, ii, 268a).† (AS)
